title: Equal Circle Overlap Calculator: Lens Area
description: Find the shared area of two equal circles with the Equal Circle Overlap Calculator — the lens area from radius and centre distance. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, two circles of radius 10 whose centres are 10 apart overlap by approx. 122.84 square units — about 39.1% of either circle.
quick_answer: The Equal Circle Overlap Calculator computes the lens-shaped area shared by two circles of the same radius whose centres are a given distance apart. Enter the radius and the centre separation and it returns the overlap area — the geometry behind coverage sharing, Venn diagrams and paired service zones.

body.t: Two transmitters, sprinklers or sensors with equal range overlap in a lens. Its area is the double-covered zone — sometimes the point, sometimes the waste.

Sprinkler heads are spaced so their circles overlap by design. The lens area tells you how much ground gets watered twice at a given spacing.
The lens (vesica) is the prettiest result in elementary circle geometry, and this calculator lets a class explore it numerically before proving it.
r = 10, d = 10: overlap = 2r² cos⁻¹(d/2r) − (d/2)√(4r² − d²) = 200 × 1.0472 − 5 × 17.32 ≈ 122.84 — 39.1% of either circle (314.16). One radius of separation still shares over a third of each circle.
r = 10, d = 14: the lens shrinks to approx. 59.10, just 18.8% of a circle. Four extra units of separation halved the sharing — the relationship is steep, which the table below maps.

faq: The circular lens formula: 2r² cos⁻¹(d ÷ 2r) − (d ÷ 2) × √(4r² − d²), for equal radii r and centre distance d. The guide on this page derives it from two circular segments.
The area common to two equal circles — nothing else, precisely. Unequal circles need the general two-circle intersection formula, a different calculation.
No. Two inputs, instant answer, nothing uploaded.
Can I use the result for professional work?
For planning sprinkler, sensor and coverage layouts, yes — the geometry is exact. Field performance (pressure, wind, terrain) then modifies what the geometry promises.
What if the centres are further apart than 2r?
The overlap is zero — the circles do not meet. The calculator reports 0 rather than a negative fiction.
What if one circle is inside the other?
With equal radii that only happens at d = 0 (full coincidence). Unequal containment belongs to the general formula.
Because the symmetric lens has the clean closed form above, and equal-radius pairs (same sprinkler model, same delivery promise) are the common practical case.
What is the overlap when d equals r?
Approx. 39.1% of either circle — the famous vesica proportion, where each centre lies on the other's circumference.
Can I use it for sprinkler spacing?
Yes: pick a target overlap share from the table, read off the d it implies for your heads' radius, and space accordingly.
